steps.tx: **Liver transplantation** (replacement of failed liver with donor organ) is definitive therapy for acute liver failure, decompensated cirrhosis and selected cancers. **Model for End Stage Liver Disease score** (MELD, bilirubin creatinine INR based) ranges 6 to 40 and allocates organs by sickness. **Living donor transplantation** (part of healthy liver) dominates in India. **Primary graft dysfunction** (failed donor liver) declares within 7 days of surgery.
steps.say: Liver transplantation replaces a failed liver with a donor organ and is definitive for acute failure and decompensated cirrhosis and selected cancers. The MELD score combines bilirubin and creatinine and clotting to range from six to forty and allocates organs by sickness. Living donor surgery with part of a healthy liver dominates in India. Failure of the new liver declares within the first week.

steps.tx: Indications are **acute liver failure** (encephalopathy with coagulopathy), decompensated cirrhosis with refractory ascites, variceal bleeding, encephalopathy or hepatorenal syndrome, and **hepatocellular carcinoma** (liver cancer) within Milan criteria. **Acute on chronic liver failure** (ACLF, acute decompensation on chronic disease) needs urgent listing. **Primary biliary cholangitis** (immune bile duct disease) and primary sclerosing cholangitis are non malignant indications with good outcomes.
steps.say: Indications include acute liver failure with brain dysfunction and clotting failure, decompensated cirrhosis with stubborn ascites or variceal bleeding or brain failure or kidney failure, and liver cancer within strict size limits. Acute on chronic failure needs urgent listing. Immune bile duct diseases are non malignant indications with good outcomes.

steps.tx: Donor safety needs blood group compatibility, graft weight above **0.8 percent** of recipient body weight and exclusion of malignancy and sepsis. **Brain death donation** (neurological criteria) provides whole livers, while living donation needs right lobe harvest with adequate remnant. **Cold ischaemia time** (storage without blood flow) stays under 12 hours for good grafts. **ABO incompatibility** (mismatched blood group) is increasingly attempted with desensitisation protocols.
steps.say: Donor assessment needs blood group compatibility and graft weight above zero point eight percent of recipient weight and exclusion of cancer and sepsis. Brain death donation provides whole livers, while living donation needs a right lobe with safe remnant. Cold storage time stays under twelve hours for good grafts. Blood group mismatched transplants are increasingly attempted with special protocols.

steps.tx: Evaluation includes cardiopulmonary clearance, **hepatocellular carcinoma staging** (tumour burden imaging), infection screen and alcohol abstinence verification. **Pulmonary hypertension** (high lung pressure) with mean pressure above 35 mmHg is usually prohibitive. **Oesophagogastric varices** (bleeding veins) and portal vein thrombosis (clotted portal vein) need reconstruction planning. Psychosocial assessment ensures adherence and support.
steps.say: Evaluation checks heart and lung fitness, tumour staging, infection screen and verified alcohol abstinence. High lung pressure above thirty five is usually prohibitive. Varices and clotted portal veins need reconstruction planning. Psychosocial assessment ensures adherence and support.

steps.tx: **Doppler ultrasound** (blood flow scan) daily monitors hepatic artery and portal vein patency. **Liver biopsy** (tissue sample) is the gold standard for rejection, showing portal inflammation and bile duct damage. **Donor lymphocyte crossmatch** (compatibility test) and cytomegalovirus status guide prophylaxis. **Cytomegalovirus prophylaxis** (preventive antiviral) with ganciclovir is standard in mismatch cases.
steps.say: Daily Doppler scans check artery and vein patency. Tissue biopsy is the gold standard for rejection. Compatibility testing and virus status guide preventive antivirals. Ganciclovir prevention is standard when donor and recipient virus status mismatch.

steps.tx: **Tacrolimus** (calcineurin inhibitor) is the backbone immunosuppressant with mycophenolate and steroids, weaned by protocol. **Induction therapy** (initial antibody suppression) with basiliximab or antithymocyte globulin covers high risk recipients. **Pneumocystis prophylaxis** (cotrimoxazole) continues for 6 months. **Enteric coated mycophenolate** (gut friendly formulation) replaces mycophenolate mofetil for tolerance. Drug levels and kidney function need lifelong monitoring.
steps.say: Tacrolimus with mycophenolate and steroids forms the backbone, weaned by protocol. Initial antibody induction covers high risk recipients. Pneumocystis prevention continues for six months. Gut friendly mycophenolate formulation improves tolerance. Drug levels and kidney function need lifelong monitoring.

steps.tx: **Acute cellular rejection** (immune attack on graft) peaks at 5 to 14 days with fever, raised enzymes and bilirubin, treated by steroid pulses. **Hepatic artery thrombosis** (clotted liver artery) causes graft necrosis and needs urgent thrombectomy or retransplantation. **Biliary complications** (strictures and leaks) present with cholestasis and need endoscopic stenting. **Recurrent hepatitis B** (viral reactivation) is prevented by immunoglobulin and antivirals.
steps.say: Acute rejection peaks at five to fourteen days with fever and raised liver tests and responds to steroid pulses. A clotted liver artery causes graft necrosis needing urgent surgery or retransplantation. Bile duct strictures and leaks need stenting. Recurrent hepatitis B is prevented with immunoglobulin and antivirals.

steps.tx: **Primary non function** (immediate graft failure) needs urgent retransplantation and is fatal without it. **Venous outflow obstruction** (Budd Chiari like graft block) presents with ascites and graft congestion. **Sepsis** (bloodstream infection) and **cytomegalovirus disease** (viral invasive disease) dominate early mortality. **Long term renal failure** (kidney failure) from calcineurin toxicity is the commonest late comorbidity. Malignancy recurrence needs surveillance imaging.
steps.say: Immediate graft failure is fatal without urgent retransplantation. Outflow block causes ascites and graft congestion. Sepsis and invasive virus disease dominate early death. Long term kidney failure from the main drug is the commonest late complication. Tumour recurrence needs surveillance imaging.

steps.tx: Overall five year graft survival exceeds **70 percent** in most Indian series, with better outcomes in living donor recipients. Hepatitis B recurrence without prophylaxis approaches 80 percent historically. **Hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence** (tumour return) after transplant exceeds 20 percent beyond Milan criteria. Living donors recover independently, with mortality below 0.5 percent in experienced centres.
steps.say: Five year graft survival exceeds seventy percent in most Indian series, with better living donor outcomes. Hepatitis B recurrence without prevention was very high historically. Tumour recurrence exceeds twenty percent beyond Milan limits. Living donors recover independently, with mortality below half a percent in experienced centres.

steps.tx: Milan criteria define transplantable **hepatocellular carcinoma** as single tumour up to 5 cm or 3 tumours up to 3 cm without vascular invasion. **Downstaging protocols** (locoregional therapy to shrink tumours) expand eligibility in trials. **Acute liver failure** listing uses King's College criteria and high lactate thresholds. Examination traps include transplanting with uncontrolled infection, ignoring pulmonary hypertension and forgetting cytomegalovirus prophylaxis in mismatch donors.
steps.say: Milan limits define transplantable liver cancer as one tumour up to five centimetres or three tumours up to three centimetres without vessel invasion. Tumour shrinking protocols expand eligibility in trials. Acute failure listing uses King's College criteria. Traps include transplanting with uncontrolled infection and forgetting virus prophylaxis in mismatch donors.

steps.tx: The **high yield table** gathers MELD allocation, rejection timing and prophylaxis rules. Acute rejection window, artery thrombosis urgency and hepatitis B prevention are the most asked points in theory and ward viva examinations. Milan criteria numbers and living donor mortality figures are repeated viva favourites that need precise recall.
steps.say: This table gathers MELD allocation and rejection timing and prophylaxis rules for revision. The acute rejection window and artery thrombosis urgency and hepatitis B prevention are the most asked points. Milan criteria numbers are repeated viva favourites.
